title: Net Worth Ledger: one number, computed from entries a human can audit
metaDescription: Assets and liabilities aggregate into a single live number with on-demand refresh and a dated history. The arithmetic happens in SQL, not in a model.
dek: A net-worth ledger that adds up assets and liabilities into one live number, with a deliberate refresh and an append-only history you can audit line by line.
intro: The Net Worth Ledger aggregates assets and liabilities into one live figure, refreshed on demand, with a dated history behind it. It is the same discipline as commission and financial reporting work: one number, computed from entries a human can audit. The arithmetic is done in code rather than by a model — totals and history are SQL, and the only model call in the picture is an occasional free-tier web lookup when a balance needs refreshing, confirmed by a human before it lands.
why: One number computed from dated entries beats a spreadsheet nobody trusts. The two rules that make that work are to store facts and compute totals rather than caching a total a model produced, and to make history append-only: if a value can be overwritten silently, the trend it sits in cannot be trusted. Refresh is a button rather than a background job precisely because these are numbers decisions get made with, so a change should be deliberate and traceable. The valuable part of finance automation is the audit trail, not the total.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Effectively nothing: an occasional free-tier model call for a balance lookup and a local database for everything else. The running cost stays near zero, which is what you want under a number you make decisions with.

faq.q: Does a model do the arithmetic?
faq.a: No. Totals and history are computed in SQL against stored entries. Never let a model do arithmetic you can do in SQL — the model's only job here is the occasional lookup, and a human confirms it.
Append, never overwrite. Every refresh adds dated entries, so the same figure can be recomputed and audited later instead of overwriting the value that was there before.

cta: This one carries personal financial data, so it is never published — the design rules are the shareable part.
